title: Corridor failover tactical notes and operator playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical scratchpad and lightweight runbook for corridor-style, partial-region failovers where a contiguous set of POPs/edges degrade (egress corridor) but other regions remain healthy. It focuses on safe traffic migration strategies, DNS/TTL coordination, KV cache considerations, and operator heuristics.

Status/context notes (short):
- Not a final runbook; this is an operator-centric playbook draft for the next SRE tabletop.
- Goal: reduce application-visible errors during corridor degradations by migrating traffic gradually to alternate region(s) while minimizing cache warmup penalty.
- Contrast with full-region evacuation: we assume control-plane and some edge POPs are responsive but experiencing elevated tail latency / packet loss.

Summary of recommended approach (high level):
1) Detect corridor onset via combined signals (edge latency spikes + increasing 5xx ratio + upstream TCP retransmits).
2) Activate protective client-side throttles and short-circuit costly retries at the edge (reduce flap).
3) Start a weighted, phased traffic rehoming to neighbor region(s) using route weight shifts in 5-10% increments every 2-5 minutes (adjust cadence based on observed error delta).
4) Pre-warm KV caches and prefix caches in target region during the weight ramp to reduce cold-cache penalty.
5) Coordinate DNS TTL changes only when routing weights near 70%+ to avoid DNS churn; prefer traffic steering (control-plane weights) as primary mechanism.

Detection and primary signals to watch (alerts we use):
- edge-latency.p99.region-xyz > 1200ms for 3m AND edge-5xx.rate > 0.5%
- cross-pop retransmit ratio > 3% (BGP & perf telemetry)
- backlog in the corridor egress queue > 80%
- client error spike with origin-connected errors (to distinguish origin vs edge failures)
If 2+ signals present, declare CORRIDOR_DEGRADING incident.

Immediate operator checklist (first 10 minutes):
- [ ] Triage: open incident in SRE and tag impacted customers (SRE-INC-XXXX).
- [ ] Notify growth/ops slack channel with short impact blurb + runbook link.
- [ ] Flip client-side non-critical retries off for 10m via config flag (minimizes retry storms).
- [ ] Change control-plane routing policy: reduce corridor weight by 15% to neighbor region A (example command below).
- [ ] Start telemetry watch: p50/p95/p99 per-route, kvcache hit ratio, new connection failures.

Weight-shift cadence (recommended):
- Phase 0 (0-5m): -15% away from corridor, watch for error delta, ensure target region latency p99 < threshold.
- Phase 1 (5-20m): incremental shifts of 5-10% every ~3 minutes with prefetch triggers at each step.
- Phase 2 (20-60m): after reaching ~60-75% shifted, initiate DNS TTL reduction if longer-term persistent shift required.
- Rollback triggers: uptick in overall latency p99 by >200ms or increase in origin 5xxs by >1% after a shift step.

KV cache prewarm strategy (operational):
- Use the control plane to trigger prefix prefetch for top N prefixes (by QPS) into target cluster. For ad-hoc: call /internal/cache/prefetch with list of prefix bundles.
- If automated prefetch not available, use synthetic traffic from canary runner to exercise hot prefixes at low QPS.
- Keep prefetch window short (2-10 min) to avoid over-eviction in target region.
- Monitor kvcache hit ratio and TTL distribution in target cluster; wait for hit ratio improvement before next weight step.

DNS and TTL guidance (notes):
- Prefer control-plane weights for initial minutes. Only change DNS TTLs if shift is expected to be longer than 30 minutes and steady-state decisions made.
- When lowering TTL to expedite client convergence, do it after weight >= 70% to avoid oscillation.
- Avoid coordinating CNAME swaps during high churn windows; prefer ALIAS/A record manipulations handled by traffic management.

Client backoff and retry behavior (safety knobs):
- Shorten client retry window from default (30s) to 5-10s for impacted routes via per-route config override during incidents.
- Enable exponential backoff with jitter for clients; disable aggressive immediate retry for non-idempotent calls.

Telemetry queries (examples to paste into dashboards):
- p99 latency by route: query latency.p99{env:prod,region:*} by region, route
- 5xx rate over 1m: sum(rate(http_server_errors_total[1m])) by (region) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m])) by (region)
- kvcache hit ratio: kvcache.hit_total / (kvcache.hit_total + kvcache.miss_total) by (cluster)

Quick operator commands (control-plane examples, adapt for your environment):
- Reduce weight for corridor (example REST call):
  curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/weights \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \
    -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","adjustments":[{"region":"eu-west-1","delta":-0.15},{"region":"eu-central-1","delta":+0.15}]}'
- Trigger prefix prefetch (internal):
  curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/internal/cache/prefetch -d '{"target_region":"eu-central-1","prefix_bundle":"hot-100"}'
- Short circuit retries via feature flag service:
  curl -X PATCH https://flags.internal/api/flags/retries-disabled -d '{"routes":["/v1/generate"],"value":true}'

Observability sanity checks after each weight step:
- overall error ratio across clusters should not increase > 0.3% absolute
- target region p99 should remain < corridor p95 (we only accept higher p50/p95 for short windows)
- kvcache miss rate in target cluster should trend downward within 10 minutes of prefetch

Rollout and rollback criteria (operator heuristics):
- Continue ramp if: global error rate stable or trending down, target p99 < corridor p95 + 200ms, kvcache miss trending down.
- Pause ramp if: global errors increase > 0.5% absolute OR target region p99 spikes > 300ms OR origin errors increase.
- Full rollback: if after a pause and quick mitigation the error state persists for > 20 minutes, revert to previous known-good weight with a slow re-introduction plan.

Post-incident analysis items (must-haves for the PIR):
- Exact time window where control-plane weight changes began and when DNS TTL changes (if any) occurred.
- Cache warmup delta: quant and qualitative (client latency vs server CPU).
- Root cause hypothesis for corridor onset (edge peering, provider-degraded links, local datacenter pressure).
- Effectiveness of retry-shortening and feature-flagging approach (did it reduce retry storm?).
- Any customer-facing impacts and communications timeline.

Open questions / follow-ups for tabletop:
- Can we automate prefix prefetch for the top-500 prefixes when weight shift > 10%? (SRE + infra action)
- Should we centralize a single control-plane endpoint for 'corridor-mode' that performs coordinated prefetch + weight plan + TTL ops? (product/infra)
- How to better detect corridor degradation earlier with less noise (probe cadence, new telemetry signals)?
- Document per-client SDK knobs to respect incident-level retry flags (SDK team task).

Appendix A: operator playbook TL;DR (for pager duty):
1) Quietly reduce corridor weight -15% to neighbor region.
2) Disable client aggressive retries.
3) Prefetch hot prefixes into target region.
4) Ramp 5-10% every 3 minutes watching p99 and kvcache hit rate.
5) If stable at >70%, consider TTL decrease and persistent DNS updates.

Appendix B: brief incident sketch example (fictional):
- 2026-02-28 08:12 UTC: edge p99 in eu-west-1 jumps to 1.6s, 5xx rate 0.9% -> alert fires.
- 08:15: SRE triage, client retries throttled, corridor weight -15% to eu-central-1.
- 08:18: kvcache prefetch started for hot-200 prefixes.
- 08:24: second ramp to -30% overall. Target kvcache hit increased from 12% -> 38% in 8m, global 5xx decreased to 0.28%.
- 08:45: steady state reached; decision to keep control-plane weights and avoid DNS TTL change.

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to vet exact control-plane payload schema with infra team; the curl examples are illustrative only.
- Consider a small operator tool that sequences the steps with built-in telemetry checks and automatic rollback on regression.
- Add a snippet to the SRE runbook library for customers on Dedicated who run custom DNS (they need explicit guidance on TTLs).

End of draft.
